description: Task guidance for presenting an end-to-end journey as ordered, expandable steps with visible progress
useWhen: the journey has a specific start and end point
the user interacts with several pieces of guidance or transactions in a specific order
steps expand to show the tasks or links that complete them
avoidWhen: the user only needs to read guidance, not take an action
there is no logical or helpful order to complete the tasks
inside a transactional service — use a multi-task (task-list) flow instead

doctrine.source: GOV.UK Design System — Step by step navigation pattern
doctrine.note: end-to-end journeys have a start and end point and complete in a specific order; steps are numbered sections the user can click to expand; tasks are links within each step; order steps by user need; use 'and'/'or' connectors between related steps; make sure the step number is read out to screen reader users
communicates the user's position in a multi-step flow — the progress semantics the journey carries
expandable content sections — the disclosure semantics for per-step task lists
sequential-step semantics for journeys read as a narrative rather than navigated step by step

knownFailureModes.note: the GOV.UK step-by-step page rebuilt in four registries produced four inconsistent substitutes; the USWDS run mapped app-step-nav to usa-process-list alone — sequential semantics but no progress indicator and no per-step disclosure
